text.p: Consumer electronic products distributor Thakral Corporation Ltd's net profit for fiscal year ended March 31, 1997 rose 20 percent to Singapore $68.6 million, company officials said on Tuesday.
The rise was within analysts' expectations of 18-20 percent growth.

Turnover rose six percent to S$1.25 billion, of which product distribution accounted for about 93 percent and manufacturing and sales six percent, the company said in a statement accompanying its results.
"We want to build that contribution (from manufacturing) up to double digits in the next couple of years," said Elie Baroudi, Thakral's deputy chief executive officer.
He told a news conferece the group intended to achieve this by fully utilising its China colour television factory, which produces 21-inch sets now, to make 25-inch and 29-inch sets.
The group saw Hong Kong and China continuing to be its main business focus.
The optimism over growth prospects in China, which accounted for more than 90 percent of its turnover, was due to its low spread of consumer electronic products.

"With the market expected to grow rapidly and reach US$24 billion by year 2000, we have set ourselves a goal of achieving a 15 percent net income growth on average over the next several years," Baroudi said.
Thakral intends to enlarge its variety of products to the full range of home appliances, including new models of wide screen televisions and video CD players.
Managing director Inderbethal Singh Thakral said the group was looking to penetrate the rural Chinese provinces like Northeastern Jilin.
"We want to expand into the rural base, strengthen ourselves in those markets where we are weak," Thakral said.
The group incurred an extraordinary loss of S$3.42 million from its cessation of the manufacturing business of associate company Wearnes Thakral.
